quotes/nyssa-evil-removed/text: In the dialogue Macrina argues that evil has no existence of its own and so cannot last forever; the fire of judgement purifies like a refiner’s fire until evil is wholly removed and God is all in all.
quotes/isaac-scourge-of-love/text: Isaac of Nineveh teaches that those in Gehenna are scourged by the scourge of love, and in his later homilies hopes that the mercy which created all things will not be defeated in the end.
quotes/julian-all-shall-be-well/text: All shall be well, and all shall be well, and all manner of thing shall be well.
quotes/talbott-inescapable-love/text: Talbott argues that a God of perfect love would never cease seeking the lost, and that since no fully informed person could have a motive to reject the source of their own happiness forever, God’s love will in the end win everyone freely.
quotes/hart-all-saved/text: Hart contends that a God who creates freely out of nothing is morally responsible for the final end of all he makes, so that eternal torment would make God’s goodness unintelligible.
quotes/fudge-destruction/text: Fudge argues that the Bible’s language of death, destruction and consuming fire means that the unsaved finally perish; immortality is God’s gift in Christ, not a natural possession of every soul.
quotes/stott-tentative-annihilation/text: Stott wrote that he held the view tentatively, but found it emotionally intolerable and exegetically unpersuasive that people could be kept in conscious torment for ever; he judged final annihilation a legitimate, biblically founded alternative.
quotes/edwards-spider/text: The God that holds you over the pit of hell, much as one holds a spider, or some loathsome insect, over the fire, abhors you, and is dreadfully provoked.
quotes/tertullian-marcion-knife/text: Marcion expressly and openly used the knife, not the pen, since he made such an excision of the Scriptures as suited his own subject-matter.
quotes/irenaeus-four-gospels/text: It is not possible that the Gospels can be either more or fewer in number than they are. For, since there are four zones of the world in which we live, and four principal winds, while the Church is scattered throughout all the world, and the ‘pillar and ground’ of the Church is the Gospel and the spirit of life; it is fitting that she should have four pillars.
quotes/irenaeus-rome-preeminent/text: For it is a matter of necessity that every Church should agree with this Church, on account of its pre-eminent authority, that is, the faithful everywhere, inasmuch as the apostolical tradition has been preserved continuously by those faithful men who exist everywhere.
quotes/athanasius-fountains-of-salvation: These are fountains of salvation, that they who thirst may be satisfied with the living words they contain. In these alone is proclaimed the doctrine of godliness. Let no man add to these, neither let him take ought from these.
quotes/basil-unwritten-tradition/text: Of the beliefs and practices whether generally accepted or publicly enjoined which are preserved in the Church some we possess derived from written teaching; others we have received delivered to us ‘in a mystery’ by the tradition of the apostles; and both of these in relation to true religion have the same force.
quotes/augustine-gospel-church-authority: For my part, I should not believe the gospel except as moved by the authority of the Catholic Church.
quotes/jerome-apocrypha-church-reads/tex: Jerome lists the books of the Hebrew canon and says that whatever is outside them is to be placed among the apocrypha; elsewhere he says the church reads Judith, Tobit and Maccabees for edification but does not use them to establish doctrine.
quotes/vincent-everywhere-always/text: Moreover, in the Catholic Church itself, all possible care must be taken, that we hold that faith which has been believed everywhere, always, by all.
quotes/luther-worms-conscience/text: Luther told the Diet that unless he were convinced by the testimony of Scripture or by clear reason — since popes and councils have often erred and contradicted themselves — he was bound by the Scriptures he had cited; his conscience was captive to the Word of God, and he could not and would not recant, since to act against conscience is neither safe nor right.
quotes/wesley-homo-unius-libri/text: O give me that book! At any price, give me the book of God! I have it: here is knowledge enough for me. Let me be homo unius libri.
quotes/pius-ix-ex-cathedra/text: Pastor Aeternus defines that when the Roman Pontiff speaks ex cathedra — defining, as pastor and teacher of all Christians, a doctrine of faith or morals to be held by the whole Church — he possesses, through divine assistance promised to Peter, the infallibility with which Christ willed his Church to be endowed, so that such definitions are irreformable of themselves and not from the consent of the Church.
quotes/dollinger-cannot-accept/text: Döllinger wrote to the Archbishop of Munich that, as a Christian, a theologian, a historian and a citizen, he could not accept the new dogma of papal infallibility, which he judged contrary to Scripture, the Fathers and the history of the Church.
quotes/warfield-inspiration/text: Hodge and Warfield argue that Scripture's inspiration extends to its words, so that the original autographs are without error in everything they affirm; an alleged error must be proved to have stood in the autograph before it counts against the doctrine.
quotes/calvin-self-authenticating/text: Calvin teaches that Scripture is self-authenticating: those inwardly taught by the Holy Spirit rest on it with certainty, and its authority does not depend on the judgement of the Church, which rather receives Scripture as the foundation on which it is built.
quotes/tertullian-happiness-marriage/tex: How shall we ever be able adequately to describe the happiness of that marriage which the Church cements, and the oblation confirms, and the benediction signs and seals; which angels carry back the news of, and the Father holds for ratified?
quotes/athenagoras-abortion-murder/text: And when we say that those women who use drugs to bring on abortion commit murder, and will have to give an account to God for the abortion, on what principle should we commit murder?
quotes/augustine-three-goods-para/text: Augustine taught that marriage has three goods: offspring (proles), faithfulness (fides) and the sacramental bond (sacramentum), which, among Christians, cannot be dissolved while both spouses live, just as the union of Christ and the Church endures.
quotes/jerome-virginity-para/text: Jerome argued against Jovinian that while marriage is good, virginity is better, comparing them, after the parable of the sower, to fruit thirtyfold and a hundredfold.
quotes/luther-estate-marriage-para/text: Luther urged that God himself instituted marriage and made man and woman for each other, so that it is a godly estate, more pleasing to him than vows of celibacy; he held that the duties of married life, even washing nappies, are holy works when done in faith.
quotes/bcp-marriage-causes/text: First, It was ordained for the procreation of children ... Secondly, It was ordained for a remedy against sin, and to avoid fornication ... Thirdly, It was ordained for the mutual society, help, and comfort, that the one ought to have of the other, both in prosperity and adversity.
quotes/humanae-vitae-para/text: Paul VI taught that the Church, calling people to observe the natural law, holds that each and every marital act must remain open to the transmission of life, because God has inseparably joined the unitive and procreative meanings of the conjugal act; recourse to infertile periods is permitted for serious reasons.
quotes/colenso-polygamy-para/text: Colenso argued that compelling a polygamous convert to send away all but one wife would break solemn obligations, cast women and children into destitution and shame, and was nowhere required by Christ or the apostles; such men should be baptised, though they should take no further wives.
quotes/stott-same-sex-para/text: Stott argued that Scripture’s teaching on sexuality rests not only on a few prohibitions but on the creation pattern of Genesis 2, where marriage is the lifelong, exclusive union of a man and a woman; he urged churches to welcome and support gay and lesbian people while calling all to chastity outside such marriage.
quotes/tutu-inclusion-para/text: Tutu argued that just as the church had been wrong to treat people unequally on account of race, it was wrong to exclude or condemn people on account of their sexual orientation, which they do not choose, and that a God of love could not endorse such discrimination.
quotes/fiducia-para/text: Fiducia Supplicans holds that couples in irregular situations, including same-sex couples, may receive a brief spontaneous blessing that asks God’s help, provided it is not liturgical and creates no confusion with marriage, which remains the exclusive, indissoluble union of a man and a woman.
quotes/benedict-idleness-enemy/text: Idleness is the enemy of the soul.
quotes/evagrius-theologian-prays/text: Evagrius taught that the one who prays truly is a theologian, and that the theologian is one who prays truly: knowledge of God is the fruit of pure prayer.
quotes/guigo-four-rungs/text: Guigo described reading as seeking the sweetness of the blessed life, meditation as finding it, prayer as asking for it and contemplation as tasting it.
quotes/francis-canticle-creatures/text: In his Canticle of the Creatures Francis praised God through "Brother Sun", "Sister Moon", wind, water, fire and "Sister Bodily Death", making all creation a choir of praise.
quotes/eckhart-rid-of-god/text: Eckhart prayed to be free of "God" as an idea or object of the mind, so as to find the Godhead in the ground of the soul where God gives birth to the Son.
quotes/kempis-day-of-judgement/text: The Imitation teaches that at the day of judgement we will be asked not what we have read but what we have done, not how well we have spoken but how devoutly we have lived.
quotes/ignatius-principle-foundation/tex: Man is created to praise, reverence, and serve God our Lord, and by this means to save his soul.
quotes/teresa-castle-diamond/text: Teresa invited her sisters to think of the soul as a castle made of a single diamond or very clear crystal, with many rooms, at whose centre God dwells; the door into it is prayer.
quotes/john-cross-dark-night-para/text: John taught that God leads the soul through a dark night in which consolations are withdrawn, not as punishment but as a loving purification that prepares it for union.
quotes/baxter-heavenly-meditation/text: Baxter urged believers to set apart a daily time to meditate on heaven, warming the heart by considering the saints’ rest and pleading with their own souls.
quotes/fox-speak-to-thy-condition/text: There is one, even Christ Jesus, that can speak to thy condition
quotes/wesley-means-of-grace-definition/: By "means of grace" I understand outward signs, words, or actions, ordained of God, and appointed for this end, to be the ordinary channels whereby he might convey to men, preventing, justifying, or sanctifying grace.
quotes/zinzendorf-heart-religion/text: Zinzendorf taught a "religion of the heart": a childlike, joyful love for the crucified Saviour felt in the heart matters more than doctrinal precision.
quotes/nicodemus-philokalia-for-all/text: Nicodemus prefaced the Philokalia by insisting that unceasing prayer and watchfulness are not only for monks but for all Christians, including lay people in the world.
